definition: The file could not be opened by the reader named in the case (crash, error, or not recognised).
The file is shorter than its own header or archive entry says it should be; the tail of the data is missing.
Headerless raw binary: size, type, byte order and layout are known only from documentation, not from the file.
A header describes the raw layout but gives no georeferencing, so readers fall back to pixel coordinates.
A sidecar (VRT, .ers, .aux.xml, world file) supplies georeferencing that does not match the data.
A VRT's raw source lies outside the VRT's directory, which current GDAL refuses unless GDAL_VRT_RAWRASTERBAND_ALLOWED_SOURCE allows it.
Discrete sampling geometry (station time series, profiles, trajectories) that raster readers present as if it were a grid.
No coordinate variables and no CRS: the grid is identifiable only from attributes, documentation or the array shape.
Positions are given only as 2D longitude and latitude arrays (no 1D axes, no grid mapping). Storage fact; whether the grid is regular in some frame is a separate question.
Confirmed: 2D longitude and latitude arrays that are exactly a regular grid in a named CRS (the case gives the fit and its residuals), so an extent and a CRS replace them.
2D longitude and latitude arrays in which longitude varies only along columns and latitude only along rows, so they reduce to two 1D axes.
2D longitude and latitude stored alongside 1D projected or rotated axes; the 1D axes and a grid mapping are the real grid, the 2D arrays are derived.
A 1D latitude axis whose spacing is uniform in Mercator y, not in degrees: a Mercator grid published as longitude and latitude.
1D axes labelled as longitude and latitude are the model's own index-space coordinates, not geographic positions.
A model grid whose pole is moved off the geographic pole; positions are regular only in the model's own transformed frame.
Several position arrays are given (centres and corners, or staggered points), and which is which is not declared.
A grid_mapping (or CRS) is declared but does not match the grid the coordinates actually describe.
A variable names a grid_mapping variable that does not exist in the file.
Projected x/y coordinates are present but no grid_mapping says which projection.
An identifier (station, catchment, region code) is stored as a coordinate, typically labelled longitude or x.
A variable's coordinates attribute names variables that do not exist in the file.
A 1D coordinate is monotonic but its spacing is not uniform (in degrees, or in Mercator y).
A 1D coordinate is not monotonic.
Coordinate arrays contain non-finite values (NaN or Inf), e.g. outside the disk of an azimuthal projection.
Longitudes run 0 to 360 rather than -180 to 180.
Longitudes exceed 360 (a grid continued past the seam).
Longitudes go below -180.
Latitude (or y) increases with row index: stored south-up, which readers must flip for a north-up image.
Related arrays in one product are stored with opposite row orders.
An array's dimensions put the x (longitude) axis before y (latitude): stored lon-major.
A reader produces a valid-looking geotransform with latitude as x and longitude as y, without warning (lon-major storage on regular axes).
The data array is stored transposed relative to its own coordinate arrays.
Fill or sentinel values are declared under non-CF attribute names, so readers don't mask them.
Sentinel values occur in the data but are not declared at all.
_FillValue, missing_value and the values actually present disagree.
Information is encoded in the values themselves (e.g. odd/even marks measured vs. predicted), which resampling destroys.
A copy offered as the same data in another format is a resampled version, not the same grid.
Character variables carry a string-length dimension that some readers drop, breaking dimension bookkeeping.
Chunks span the whole band (time) dimension, so reading one band reads the whole file.
A store's groups cannot be listed (e.g. no consolidated metadata and no listing permission).
Time units reference year 0 or a non-decodable origin, so calendars and libraries refuse them.
A file the documentation says is included is absent.
The only statement of the dimensions, type or layout is in prose documentation.
